title: Cross-Chirality Generalization by Axial Vectors for Hetero-Chiral Protein-Peptide Interaction Design
claim: Flipping chirality lets a model trained on one handedness design the other, using axial features that distinguish chirality.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, zoom-in from system to module to features
description: Four-column figure with green headings. Far left shows L-protein/L-binder and D-protein/D-binder structure pairs, connected by 'Flip' double arrows, in orange and blue-lavender ribbon renderings. Next is a latent diffusion block: an encoder trapezoid, 'Forward diffusion' arrow over two rows of dot-cluster boxes running from t=0 to t=T, and a decoder trapezoid with a 'Denoising' arrow back. Third is the AFI-EPT module, a stacked layer with Attention, an 'Axial Feat. Injection' box in red, and a GVP-FFN, with H and V inputs and outputs. The right column has three cream panels with 3D vector diagrams for u×v, a triple-product feature and a commutator feature, each shown before and after inversion with norm-versus-angle sinusoid insets. Orange-red marks the axial features.
caption: We use chiral-sensitive model PepMirror to design D-peptides by flipping. PepMirror is a latent diffusion model using AFI-EPT, which injects axial vector features to learn the chirality. Axial vectors are invariant under the spatial inversion, and we give three direct constructions. The commutator feature (third) captures higher frequency information of the angle between u, v.
abstract: D-peptide binders targeting L-proteins have promising therapeutic potential. Despite rapid advances in machine learning-based target-conditioned peptide design, generating D-peptide binders remains largely unexplored. In this work, we show that by injecting axial features to $E(3)$-equivariant (polar) vector features, it is feasible to achieve cross-chirality generalization from homo-chiral (L--L) training data to hetero-chiral (D--L) design tasks. By implementing this method within a latent diffusion model, we achieved D-peptide binder design that not only outperforms existing tools in \textit{in silico} benchmarks, but also demonstrates efficacy in wet-lab validation. To our knowledge, our approach represents the first wet-lab validated generative AI for the \textit{de novo} design of D-peptide binders, offering new perspectives on handling chirality in protein design. Codes are available at https://github.com/YZY010418/PepMirror
